title: Rewrite presubmit lint bootstrapping into TypeScript composite action and add presubmit telemetry + dependency-prune snapshotter
author: Sofia Chen
release_notes: Improve presubmit boot time, add presubmit telemetry for CI observability, introduce a dependency-prune snapshotter to identify and safely remove stale dev-dependencies. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: our existing presubmit bootstrap (bash + make) has become brittle, slow on cold runners, and hard to reuse across repos. This PR rewrites the presubmit bootstrapping into a small TypeScript composite action (ts-presubmit-bootstrap) that runs deterministically in the Actions runtime, plus a lightweight presubmit-telemetry exporter that emits granular metrics (bootstrap duration, cache-hit, step-latency) to our internal metrics sink. Additionally it introduces tools/dep-pruner: a safe snapshotter that detects unused devDependencies across monorepo packages, generates suggested removals, and provides an opt-in auto-PR mode. Changes are intended to be incremental and opt-in; the new action is published but the old bootstrap is still available under a deprecation flag for 30 days. Checklist: [x] TypeScript composite action with unit tests, [x] Presubmit telemetry exporter and documentation, [x] dep-pruner scanner with dry-run and auto-pr mode, [x] Team docs and migration guide, [x] Benchmarks and CI runs. Summary of impact: - Cold presubmit bootstrap time reduced from ~28s to ~8s on average (measured across 50 ephemeral runners) - Median lint pipeline start time improved by ~400ms due to reduced shell init overhead - Identified ~62 dev-deps across the repo that are likely unused (report generated), with 18 safe removals applied via the auto-PR mode during the branch run. Rollout plan: land behind feature flag, run presubmit-telemetry for 2 weeks, open dep-pruner suggestions to team leads, then enable auto-PR for low-risk changes. Related work: ENG-1324 (presubmit refactor), ENG-1409 (ci telemetry), SUP-778 (support churn from long runner boot times).

review_comments: Marcus Li: Can we keep a short-lived compatibility shim so teams can opt in incrementally? Suggest a 'USE_TS_BOOTSTRAP' env flag in presubmit.yml.

Sofia Chen (author): Good call — added the flag and documented it in the migration guide. The composite action registers as 'ts-presubmit-bootstrap@v1' and will only be used when USE_TS_BOOTSTRAP=true.
Aisha Patel: The telemetry schema looks fine but please avoid emitting any repo-scoped filenames that could contain PII. Also add a sampling hook for noisy repos.
Sofia Chen (author): Removed filename tags from payload and added a sampling config (default 1%). Documented telemetry privacy in docs/ci/telemetry.md.
Diego Morales: dep-pruner found many candidates; ensure we have a human-in-the-loop for anything non-dev-only. Recommend auto-PR only for packages with a single consumer.
Sofia Chen (author): Auto-PR is opt-in and defaulted to dry-run. Added heuristics to restrict auto-PRs to dev-only packages with 1 consumer and no transitive usage flagged by run-time traces.
Marcus Li: unit tests flaked on macOS runners; changed the tempdir strategy in tests, that resolved it. Approving pending green CI.
CI Bot: All required checks passed on re-run.

performance_notes: Benchmark harness: 50 ephemeral runners across actions-hosting (ubuntu-latest). Cold start median decreased from 28s->8s; 95th percentile from 90s->22s. Presubmit telemetry provides per-run breakdown to reproduce regressions.
safety_and_rollout: Feature gated: new action behind USE_TS_BOOTSTRAP flag. dep-pruner runs in dry-run mode by default. Auto-PR occurs only when the repo-maintainer label is present and heuristics agree. Dep removals will be batched and annotated for traceability.
